claims.text: Group IV-containing refractory high-entropy alloys are highly susceptible to oxygen uptake during processing.
Oxygen uptake drives precipitation of brittle alpha-HCP phases in Group IV-containing RHEAs.
Brittle alpha-HCP precipitation raises the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
Decomposing hydride precursors under vacuum below 10^-6 torr will prevent oxygen uptake.
Heating to 1200°C at more than 100°C/min followed by immediate extrusion will suppress alpha-HCP nucleation.
The proposed vacuum-assisted rapid extrusion process will produce a dense, crack-free bulk RHEA.
The proposed process will enhance high-temperature yield strength relative to conventional extrusion.
Surface oxidation of hydrides or powder handling can elevate the initial oxygen content.
Avoiding prolonged exposure to intermediate temperatures limits oxygen diffusion.
An extrusion strain rate optimized for dynamic recrystallization will aid successful consolidation.
Extrusion above 1000°C provides adequate plasticity without phase segregation.
Rapid cooling and low oxygen activity stabilize a metastable single-phase BCC solid solution.
The proposed processing route prevents formation of brittle Al-Zr-based intermetallics and oxide inclusions.
Hydrogen released during hydride decomposition acts as a transient lattice dilator.
Rapid heating and extrusion outpace diffusion-limited oxidation and phase-separation processes.
A metastable BCC structure provides high yield strength at elevated temperatures.
The processed alloy will contain less than 100 ppm oxygen.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength exceeding 500 MPa at 1000°C.
Conventional hydride decomposition and extrusion in argon or air causes oxygen uptake, alpha-HCP precipitation, and catastrophic cracking.
Alpha-HCP formation is a known failure mode in refractory high-entropy alloys containing Ti, Zr, or Hf.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 torr, while the conditions present argon with less than 80 ppm O2 as an alternative even though the baseline describes argon processing as causing oxygen uptake and embrittlement.

The proposed treatment specifies heating to 1200°C and extrusion above 1000°C, but the falsification experiment extrudes both batches at exactly 1000°C, so it does not test the stated thermal history.
